searchText: There is some confusion about the latest ethereum/tests release (cc <@259648573401071617>): 1. The EIPTests/StateTests/stEIP2537 contains outdated tests for BLS precompiles. These probably should be completely deleted. 2. ethereum/tests imports EEST in `Pyspecs` directories, but I don't see Prague tests there. Thanks for reporting, cc <@393119312350543872> About 2. I would recommend running EEST tests from EEST release tarballs, not from ethereum/tests. EEST will probably release more frequently than ethereum/tests. There's a new EEST release planned for later today, btw. I agree on this and this is what evmone is doing (I recommend to keep the list of the test sources in a CI config, not as git submodules). That's why my opinion is to remove any EEST tests from ethereum/tests not to give false sense of "all tests are here". (it will also save me time executing the same tests twice 😉 ) I agree here, tests should move one way (ethereum/tests -> EEST) and not the other way around or both 🙂 Biggest contribution ever: https://github.com/ethereum/tests/pull/1466 Now let's review this PR line-by-line 🙂 some teams prefer to have repo with .json to tar balls. I would suggest reorganizing releases into ethereum/tests after we clean up all .json fillers ok. to avoid confusion about pyspec vectors I think it is better to keep it at one place https://github.com/ethereum/tests/pull/1467 is everyone ok with that ? Purge away! that was the only verification of json schema consistency ( 🧪 EEST **v4.1.0** release! Predominantly adds additional coverage for EIP-2357. Please bump to this version in your EL client CI. https://github.com/ethereum/execution-spec-tests/releases/tag/v4.1.0

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content:
There is some confusion about the latest ethereum/tests release (cc <@259648573401071617>):
1. The EIPTests/StateTests/stEIP2537 contains outdated tests for BLS precompiles. These probably should be completely deleted.
2. ethereum/tests imports EEST in `Pyspecs` directories, but I don't see Prague tests there.

excerpts.author: danceratopz
excerpts.content: About 2. I would recommend running EEST tests from EEST release tarballs, not from ethereum/tests. EEST will probably release more frequently than ethereum/tests. There's a new EEST release planned for later today, btw.

excerpts.author: chfast
excerpts.content: I agree on this and this is what evmone is doing (I recommend to keep the list of the test sources in a CI config, not as git submodules). That's why my opinion is to remove any EEST tests from ethereum/tests not to give false sense of "all tests are here". (it will also save me time executing the same tests twice 😉 )

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: I agree here, tests should move one way (ethereum/tests -> EEST) and not the other way around or both 🙂

excerpts.author: jochembrouwer
excerpts.content: Now let's review this PR line-by-line 🙂
